questions.questionsTitle: Choose the correct option and complete the statements

subQuestion.question: (1) A system of independent and sovereign states _________.
(2) The main responsibility of the League of Nations _________.
(3) The Cold War ended with this event _________.

questions.questionsTitle: Explain with reasons whether the following statements are true or false

subQuestion.question: (1) The League of Nations was established after the First World War.
subQuestion.ans:
(1) The First World War caused a tremendous loss of life and property.

                    (2) All the nations felt that such a war should not happen again and some measures need to be taken to achieve this end.

                    (3) Out of this thinking, an international organisation called the ‘League of Nations’ was established to solve international disputes and to avoid war.

subQuestion.question: (2) The world became unipolar due to the Cold War.
subQuestion.ans:
(1) An international system in which there is only one super power and several countries are dependent on it, is called ‘Unipolar System’.

                    (2) Due to the cold war, most of the countries of the world joined either of the power blocs headed by the two super powers.

                    (3) Such a division of nations in two groups is called ‘bipolarisation’. Thus, the world became bipolar and not unipolar due to the Cold War.

subQuestion.question: (3) The policies of Mikhail Gorbachev gave an impetus to democratisation.
subQuestion.ans:
(1) The President of the Soviet Russia, Mikhail Gorbachev implemented the policies of Perestroika (Restructuring) and Glasnost (Openness).

                    (2) Due to these policies, the control over the media was reduced. Important changes took place in political and economic spheres.

                    (3) The economic and political spheres were restructured. This gave impetus to democracy. Thus, the policies of Mikhail Gorbachev gave an impetus to democratisation.

subQuestion.question: (1) Cold War:
subQuestion.ans:
(1) After the Second World War, both countries – America and Soviet Russia became competitors to increase their hegemony (influence).

                    (2) There was no actual war between these two countries, but the tensions in the circumstances were such that they could be responsible for causing war.

                    (3) The conflict between the superpowers, the struggle for power, the arms race and the attitude of checkmating each other created an environment conducive to war. This war-like situation is described as ‘Cold War’.

subQuestion.question: (2) Non-alignment:
subQuestion.ans:
(1) The cold war that started after the Second World War divided the world into two groups of superpowers.

                    (2) There were some countries which did not want to join the superpower rivalry.

                    (3) The policy of these nations to remain away from the competition of superpowers is called ‘non-alignment’.

subQuestion.question: (3) Interdependence:
subQuestion.ans:
(1) All the countries of the world are dependent on each other for one reason or the other. This is called interdependence.

                    (2) The undeveloped nations have to depend on developed countries.

                    (3) Even big nations have to depend upon other big and small nations for trade.

                    (4) However big, prosperous or developed a nation may be, it can never be self-sufficient about all its needs. Thus, interdependence is an important feature of the international system.

subQuestion.question: (4) Bipolarisation:
subQuestion.ans:
(1) After the Second World War, Soviet Russia became a superpower by developing nuclear weapons and increasing its military power.

                    (2) America was already a superpower.

                    (3) The nations of the world were divided into two groups of these superpowers. This division itself is called ‘bipolarisation’.

                    (4) Due to this bipolarisation, the scope of the Cold War increased, and the sphere of tension spread.

subQuestion.question: (5) Globalisation:
subQuestion.ans:
(1) After the disintegration of Soviet Russia, there was openness in trade among nations and economic relations.

                    (2) Capital, labour, market, information and ideas freely spread throughout the world.

                    (3) Due to the revolution in information technology, different events and developments began to be known everywhere.

                    (4) The boundary between nations did not remain as important as they were before, and the world itself became one big market. All these processes are together called ‘globalisation’.

questions.questionsTitle: Answer the following questions in brief

subQuestion.question: (1) What were the factors responsible for the end of the Cold War?
subQuestion.ans:
(1) The Soviet Russia adopted the policy of opening up the economy and loosening the state control on the economy.

                    (2) The then president of the Soviet Russia, Mikhail Gorbachev implemented the policy of Perestroika (Restructuring) and Glasnost – (Openness). The Soviet economy and polity were restructured.

                    (3) He reduced control over the press. This gave impetus to democracy in Russia.

                    (4) The East European countries challenged ‘socialist’ governments. These countries broke free from the influence of the Soviet Russia and adopted a democratic capitalist path.

                    (5) Disintegration of the Soviet Russia contributed to end the cold war.

subQuestion.question: (2) What are the major changes that occur in the global politics after the end of the Cold War?
subQuestion.ans:
(1) With the disintegration of Soviet Russia, America remained the only super power in world politics.

                    (2) A conducive atmosphere prevailed for the growth in trade and economic relations between and among nations.

                    (3) The United Nations, established in the post-war period, had increased responsibility for maintaining world peace and security.

                    (4) Environmental protection, fostering of human rights, gender equality, and management of natural calamities have now acquired importance globally.
